text: On June 19, 2026, the Obama Presidential Center opened to the public.
Juneteenth, the day that marks the end of slavery in America.
The night before, an invitation-only dedication brought Bruce Springsteen and Stevie Wonder to the lawn, with three former presidents in the crowd.
Then the doors opened on Jackson Park.
This is the same ground Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux laid out in 1871.
It's the same ground that held the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition, the White City that drew twenty-seven million visitors to the lakefront.
A century and a third later, a new institution sits on it.
The date was chosen on purpose.
Juneteenth, on the South Side where Barack Obama once worked as a community organizer, for a center built to honor the first Black president.
The firm Tod Williams Billie Tsien Architects designed it, with the park landscape shaped by Michael Van Valkenburgh.
At the center stands a stone museum tower that rises about 225 feet, its sides carved with words drawn from Black history.
On the north face, the artist Julie Mehretu set 35 painted glass panels she calls Uprising of the Sun, inspired by the marches from Selma to Montgomery.
The whole thing cost roughly 850 million dollars in private money.
No presidential center has ever cost that much.
Inside there's a museum, a branch of the Chicago Public Library, a forum building for public events, an athletic center, and the offices of the Obama Foundation.
